children: The S&P 500 faces the risk of an 8% to 10% correction as the Federal Reserve prepares for a potential new rate-hike cycle, according to Macro Risk Advisors founder Dean Curnutt, who warns that higher borrowing costs could squeeze corporate margins and deliver a volatility shock to a market unprepared for tighter policy.
We expect an 8-10% pullback in S&P with a potential second leg in December, Curnutt said in a Monday note to clients, according to Bloomberg.

The warning comes at a vulnerable moment. The S&P 500 has slipped nearly 1% so far in September as elevated energy prices and persistent inflation have pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level in nearly two decades.

Markets are now almost fully pricing in a quarter-point Fed hike, versus roughly 60% odds a week earlier. The Fed's Sept. 15-16 meeting concludes Wednesday, with its policy announcement scheduled for 2 p.m. ET.
Curnutt argues higher rates will compress margins in companies that cannot pass costs through while introducing a volatility shock as investors adjust to a renewed tightening cycle.
That year, the S&P 500 peaked in September, then dropped roughly 10% through October and November before another wave of selling in December pushed the decline from the peak toward 20%.
The Santa Claus rally did not come, Curnutt said.
He believes a similar second leg could emerge this December as multiple rate hikes hit into a K-shaped, low-churn economy.
What S&P 500 investors should watch next

Wednesday's Fed decision is only the first catalyst. Investors should focus on whether policymakers signal additional hikes, how the 10-year Treasury yield responds and whether companies begin cutting margin or earnings expectations.
Those signals matter particularly for richly valued growth stocks, where higher discount rates can pressure valuations even if earnings remain healthy.

Curnutt's 2018 comparison is not a forecast that history must repeat, but an 8% to 10% decline would be substantial after a strong market run. If yields keep climbing and earnings revisions weaken simultaneously, his bearish scenario would gain credibility.
For now, Curnutt's conclusion is clear: a defensive posture is the correct approach.

title: S&P 500 Faces Stark 2018 Warning as Fed Tightens
